As an individual enhances their own computing skills they become acquainted with simula-
tion through management gaming and through introduction to operation research methods,
also referred to as management science. At the same time technological improvements (such
as parallel processing platforms), advances in decision support systems, new language para-
digms (object oriented as well as functional), and simulation extensions or modular add-ons
for database management, all indicate that simulation has evolved from a research tool of last
resort to a methodology of preference. Simulation studies are becoming more cost effective,
with acceptable reliability, more end-user friendly, and more understandable.

48.1 i ntroduction
This chapter is a short descriptive tour through a hypothetical research study. The purpose
of the vignette is to point out tips of advice on practical issues the researcher should prac-
tice while conducting research. The vignette presented is resolved through experimentation.
Experimentation has broad applications in the computing field.
48.2 t he v ignette s etting
A commercial software design and development firm is concerned about how to ensure
product quality efficiently to their customer base. As a result the corporate management
board has placed several of the software design and development personnel on a team to
identify and determine which aspects of attributes prompt meeting delivery deadlines and
produce quality software in their industry. Clearly, the answer can be derived from several
diverse viewpoints and motives.
Any good software project manager would take attribute measurements of the process and
product in order to forecast delivery time and the expected budget. Customers would per-
form a feature analysis of the product with respect to their requirements and make an assess-
ment of adequate quality. Corporate management would need to determine if upgrades
were needed for meeting customer satisfaction.
Is this project noteworthy?
The effectiveness of research demands depend greatly on the proper selection of projects. In
the corporate world top level management should play a part in the project selection process
due to the fact that the benefits from research projects cross functional and business func-
tion boundaries. Therefore, since this vignette is hypothetical, this project has been deter-
mined to be noteworthy and already passed the first hurdle in becoming a research study.
Select Research Projects Carefully.
48.3 p reliminary r esearch s tudy s tatement
Anyone that has participated in a software development project, whether as a student or a
professional, knows that screening and reporting relevant data on pertinent attributes and
development processes of the software relate to the answer. The study team’s past experi-
ences would make them keenly aware that there must be an assessment of participant’s
progress in any project as well as assessment of the product’s quality. Most of the study team
would consider the variety of measurement techniques used by a software engineer.
Integrate your experiences and educational background into the research study.

48.4 b ackground r eview
A thorough background review should be immediately initiated: a literature search, both
an internet and web search, commercial software development shop visitations, interview/
questionnaire surveys of successful/experienced software development project personnel,
and any other creative ideas of searching for information. Identification of academic and
professional societies pertinent to the study would be necessary. Also identification of key
individuals or experts within the field of the study would be required.
The participants in the background study need answers for:
What are the attributes of concern?
What is the impact of the attributes of concern on software development?
Who are some of the nationally known experts in the domain of software development mea-
surement?
Which professional / academic societies are pertinent to the study?
Are there any available RFPs applicable to the study?
Each team member should list at least 6 researchable questions for future research projects
in the study domain.

chunks.title: researchmethodsforinformationsystems
chunks.heading: 48.5 Formulating a p roject that can be r esolved
chunks.sectionTitle: Formulating a p roject that can be r esolved
chunks.content:
48.5 Formulating a p roject that can be r esolved
For the sake of illustration, let’s assume that the study team has settled on using software
product metrics and software development process metrics. The team has reached agree-
ment that two major merits for product metrics are that product quality is measureable and
product attribute characteristics are quantifiable.
Goodness criteria for the product is a very controllable and well-defined domain, especially
in software engineering. However, the process metrics area is overwhelming and as a result,
the research team would be aware that it is absolutely necessary to complete both a Joint
Application Development (JAD) session and pilot testing of candidate attributes and poten-
tial analysis models.
JAD is a technique for including users in the development of a new system. The JAD sessions
are generally conducted in specially configured rooms, with the final outcome being general
agreement between users and system professionals as to general information requirements
of the business. JAD sessions are extremely appropriate during system planning and system
analysis phases of the software development life cycle (SDLC). This would be a perfect
technique to use in the study since the members of the study team would be so familiar with
it. JAD sessions would enable the study team, corporate management, customer representa-
tives, and other stakeholders to reach a consensus on attributes, metrics, and preliminary
analysis methods/models to be included in the study. A brief list of attributes would probably
626 n n n r e S earch Metho DS F or In F or M at I on Sy S te MS n ch apter 48
contain: productivity cost and resource requirements, effectiveness of quality, effectiveness
of development tools, and many others.
To complicate matters more is the fact that current software metrics are specific to a given
phase of the SDLC. For example the lines of code (LOC) can be used to measure the amount
of work done and predict size, but not before the project implementation phase begins. LOC
is commonly used to measure productivity. The study team could even consider using LOC
to measure quality. Detection of defaults is relevant only during the specification phase.
By this time the study team would realize that the project could get out of hand; downsizing
to make the study realistic as well as ensure that precise and accurate results be generated
might be required.
Always remember, be patient and strive for simplicity.
Be careful that the real problem is uncovered and solved rather than dealing with
symptoms of the actual problem.
Do not be a Robinson Crusoe, the world’s first system analyst. At one point of his island
story, he set out to build a dugout canoe. He located a fantastic tree in the exact center of the

chunks.title: researchmethodsforinformationsystems
chunks.heading: 48.5 Formulating a p roject that can be r esolved
chunks.sectionTitle: Formulating a p roject that can be r esolved
chunks.content:
island. A fabulous canoe was manufactured by the obsessive Crusoe, but to no avail. It was
literally impossible to transport the final product to water. Another failed project! Research-
ers must realize that they do not need to construct an eight lane highway for someone’s
driveway at their private home.
48.6 a ttribute s creening
Guidelines and processes that will alleviate the attribute screening could require that:
1. Attribute Measurement is dependent upon the SDLC phases.
2. Scope and cost are among the most pertinent attributes, especially for measuring
aspects of product quality.
3. Should internal attributes, which are only directly measurable, or external attributes
be selected for the study?
At this juncture, it would be apparent that a pilot study should be implemented to finalize
the attribute list and investigate various models for the data analysis. The pilot study charge
should be to find out the answers to these questions for any available and accessible data.
Is the data meaningful?
What is the origin of the data?
Is the data complete?
Is the data understandable?
Is the data pertinent to the research?
Does the data meet the requirements for the proposed preliminary analysis methods?

During these past components of the study, team members should not let themselves be
sidetracked! During screening, team members may have asked: ‘Is there a way to character-
ize metrics that may be directly related to quality, productivity, and technology?’ This would
be a great research project.
Several team members might have asked: ‘Should the firm invest in implementing efficient
fault tolerant software?’ Fault tolerance is a software/hardware technique where interven-
tion and prevention for system failures is employed. For example, defensive programming
based on redundancy can be used to cope with mistakes in the real environment. All software
faults result from design errors. Therefore, to implement fault tolerant computing for coping
with design faults, programs need to be tested repeatedly during run time and designed to
dynamically recover from errors. The fundamental method for implementing software fault
tolerance uses redundancy or alterations.
Consider the typical sort processing example. Assume that the software system allocates one
controller block, one recording block, and three sorting blocks to complete the sort. Each
request cycle begins with the controller block providing a copy of the original data file to the
first sorting block to sort. After this sorting block finishes sorting, a request is sent from the
controller block to the recording block to check whether the result is correct based upon
pre-established specifications. If this sorting block fails to produce the specified result, the
controller block will send another copy of the original data file to a different sorting block,
then begins execution. This process is repeated until the data is correctly sorted or no more
sorting blocks are available. In the latter case, the system fails.
Care must be taken; clearly, such activity by the study team indicates the team would have
become side-tracked.
Be patient!
Stay focused!
In the solution of a research study, new research projects are discovered.
Do not be discouraged, simply file these questions in your conceptual framework. These
research questions could become some of your future research studies. Congratulations
would be in order for the study team members!
Continuously build and enhance your conceptual domain.
Remember the three Ps.
Plan, prepare and then produce.
After completion of a well-defined pilot testing, attribute testing, and successful JAD ses-
sions the study team probably should have completed 90% of the overall study.
